s:
A company hosts a Git repository in an on-premises data center. The company uses webhooks to

invoke functionality that runs in the AWS Cloud. The company hosts the webhook logic on a set of Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group that the company set as a target for an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The Git server calls the ALB for the configured webhooks. The company wants to move the solution to a serverless architecture. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
o: For each webhook, create and configure an AWS Lambda function URL. Update the Git servers to call the individual Lambda function URLs.
Create an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API. Implement each webhook logic in a separate AWS Lambda function. Update the Git servers to call the API Gateway endpoint.
Deploy the webhook logic to AWS App Runner. Create an ALB, and set App Runner as the target. Update the Git servers to call the ALB endpoint.

Containerize the webhook logic. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster, and run the webhook logic in AWS Fargate. Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API, and set Fargate as the target. Update the Git servers to call the API Gateway endpoint.

w.y: Webhooks are simple HTTPS callbacks, so the winner is the serverless option with the least to run. An API Gateway HTTP API in front of one Lambda function per webhook replaces the ALB and EC2 fleet with fully managed pieces and gives the Git server a single endpoint. Lambda function URLs (A) are an even lighter option that AWS itself suggests for webhook handlers, which is why this question is debated.

o.A: Debated: function URLs are built-in HTTPS endpoints AWS suggests for simple webhooks, but each webhook gets its own URL to manage and secure; the long-standing key prefers B.
o.B: Key answer: an HTTP API plus one Lambda function per webhook is fully serverless, cheap and gives the Git server one managed endpoint.
o.C: An ALB is not serverless and has to be run separately; App Runner does not need an ALB in front of it.
o.D: Containerizing and running Fargate behind a REST API is much more work, and API Gateway REST APIs cannot target Fargate directly.

Announcing AWS Lambda Function URLs: Built-in HTTPS Endpoints for Single-Function Microservices

nt: Debated. AWS lists webhook handlers as a typical use for Lambda function URLs (A), which have even less to operate. B is the long-standing key and the safer exam pick when several webhooks share one endpoint; know both.
